tossups.text: The narrator of a novel by this author receives an accordion from the Caretaker of the Power Station in the Woods. In a story by this author, a couple attacks a McDonald's in the middle of the night after failing to find an available bakery. In one of his novels, the narrator flees from the INKlings while traveling in the sewers and gives a unicorn skull to an unnamed librarian. This author wrote about a hitwoman who enters an alternate universe after listening to Janáček's ("yah-NAH-check's") Sinfonietta in a taxi. In a novel by this author, the data-stealing Semiotecs target the data-shuffling Calcutecs. This author of The Elephant Vanishes wrote a novel in which Toru looks back on his relationships with Naoko and Midori. For 10 points, Hardboiled Wonderland and the End of the World, 1Q84, and Norwegian Wood are novels by what Japanese novelist?

A novel by this man makes fun of sentimental fiction and plagiarizes a long love story from Tristram Shandy. One of his dialogues centers on the Querelle des Bouffons[keh-RELL day boo-FAW] and is set in the chess players' Regency Café. The title servant of one of his books took a bullet to the knee but still insists that everything is written on a "great scroll" in the sky. He worked with a physicist who wrote a "Preliminary Discourse" placing all of human knowledge into three branches. Jacques the Fatalist and Rameau's Nephew were written by-for 10 points-what French Enlightenment philosophe, who co-edited the Encyclopédie with d'Alembert?

This composer created a piece in which the melody is to be played higher in its "B" section. He collaborated with Arthur Marshall on Swipesy Cakewalk and composed an opera in which the protagonist refuses to buy a "bag of luck." That opera is Treemonisha, and, in his most famous form, he composed a piece popularized by the film, The Sting. For 10 points, name this American composer of The Entertainer who pioneered a form of music exemplified in his Maple Leaf Rag, ragtime.

Vaĭnshteĭn and Zel'dovich modeled these systems using cycles of stretching, twisting, and folding. The intensity and shape of a phenomenon (emphasize) generated by one of these systems is predicted by the Glatzmaier-Roberts model. The SOHO ("soh-hoh") project provided further evidence that one of these systems is located in a tachocline, a region where solid body rotation gives way to differential rotation. In the Babcock-Leighton model of one of these systems, active regions decay to create a surface poloidal field. Eleven-year cycles are evident when plotting the intensity of the phenomenon produced by one of these systems at different latitudes on Maunder's butterfly diagrams. For 10 points, name these self-sustaining systems of electrically conducting fluids that generate magnetic fields.
acceptableAnswers: plasmas before “fluids” by asking “as a component of what systems?”
planets by asking “what system inside those bodies?”

tossups.text: The virtual form of this quantity occurs due to an object's constraints. The relativistic type of one form of this quantity is multiplied by quantity gamma minus 1. For a rigid body in two dimensions, this quantity is the time integral of a couple times angular velocity. This quantity changes sign based on the directions of cyclic processes. A path integral in a force field gives this quantity. Because the centripetal acceleration is always tangent to an object in circular motion, rotating objects do not "do" this quantity. This quantity is not torque, but it has units of Newton-meters. For 10 points, name this product of force and distance.

The unfinished Manchester Madonna is attributed to this artist. This student of Ghirlandaio painted a group of nudes frolicing in the background of his sole surviving panel painting, the Doni Tondo. This artist's final fresco is The Crucifixion of Saint Peter. This artist included a Libyan and Cumean Sibyl in a building that houses many of his paintings. Daniele da Volterra painted fig leaves over one of this artist's works to cover up the nudity. That work by this artist includes a self portrait as the flayed skin in the hands of Saint Bartholomew. For 10 points, identify this Renaissance artist who painted a Last Judgment in the Sistine Chapel.

Judith Farr suggested that this poet frequently signed letters "Your gnome" to highlight that their poetic gift was dealing in maxims. In one work this poet described how "Jamaicas of Remembrance stir / that send me reeling in." In one poem this writer described how "Impossibility, like Wine / Exhilarates the Man / Who tastes it". In that poem "Not all the Frankfort Berries / Yield such an Alcohol" because "I taste a liquor never brewed." The subject of one of their poems is "Unmoved - she notes the Chariots - pausing - / At her low Gate -" and "shuts the Door - / To her divine Majority". For 10 points name this American poet whose poem "the soul selects her own society" described her isolation in Amherst, Massachusetts.

This leader's 1969 White Paper gave full citizenship to natives. During an election this leader won against Robert Stanfield, voters were impressed when they remained seated while being pelted by rocks and bottles at a Saint-Jean-Baptiste Day parade. This leader criticized Bill 101 for its implementation of one single official language, which contradicted this leader's Official Languages Act. This leader's policy of bilingualism established equality between English and the majority language of the province he hailed from. This leader declared "Just watch me" before invoking the War Measures Act during the October Crisis. For 10 points, name this Canadian leader and father of the current prime minister, Justin.

A man with this surname names a 1989 case upholding a Missouri law restricting public funding for abortions. Profiles in Courage praises a senator with this surname for a speech defending the Compromise of 1850, in which he spoke not as "a Northern man, but as an American." In 1784, a man with this surname published the popular "blue-backed speller," which omitted silent u's. A secretary of state with this surname negotiated a treaty that settled the U.S.' northeastern border with Lord Ashburton and composed the "Great Triumvirate" with two southern senators. For 10 points, give the surname of the Massachusetts senator Daniel.

The title figure of a poem by this author "[raises] up her head, / From the darkness dread & drear" and demands, "break this heavy chain." The speaker's wrath "grew both day and night / Till it bore an apple bright" in a poem by this author that ends with the narrator's foe "outstretched beneath" a Poison Tree. This man described a figure who "gave thee clothing of delight, / Softest clothing wooly bright" in a poem that asks, "Dost thou know who made thee?" Another poem from this author's Songs of Innocence and of Experience addresses the title creature "In the forests of the night." For 10 points, name this English poet of "The Lamb" and "The Tyger."

A song in this genre briefly quotes "Ol' Man River" on the trombone and saxophone, echoing its opening lyrics, "Show me that river / Take me across." A series of rigid drum-taps followed by a trumpet fanfare introduce the title track of an album in this genre whose cover depicts a man in a blue suit walking in front of a yellow circle on a red background. Since the development of this genre roughly coincided with its country's independence, that event inspired many songs in this genre, including "Forward March" by Derrick Morgan. This genre influenced many later genres with a characteristic rhythm created by a staccato guitar upstroke played on the offbeats, as featured in the song "Wash Wash" by Prince Buster. Lynn Taitt slowed down the rhythm of this genre to create rocksteady music. This genre was fused with punk in a 1990s revival by American bands like Sublime and Reel Big Fish. For 10 points, name this Jamaican musical genre, a predecessor of reggae.

Byron White's dissent in this case argued that the decision formed "a constitutional barrier to state efforts to protect human life." In a follow-up to this case, Sandra Day O'Connor argued for the legality of legislation that did not cause an "undue burden." The Hyde Amendment and the Webster decisions were responses to this case. Harry Blackmun's opinion in this case stated Norma McCorvey's right to privacy allowed a certain action. Doe v. Bolton was decided alongside, for 10 points, what Supreme Court decision establishing a Constitutional right to abortions?

The canonical form of this quantity is equal to the derivative of the Lagrangian with respect to the time derivative of a generalized coordinate. This quantity is equal to the Fourier transform of position. According to Hamilton's equations, the time derivative of this quantity is equal to the negative derivative of the Hamiltonian with respect to its conjugate coordinate. The kinetic energy of a particle is equal to the square of this quantity divided by two times the mass of the particle. According to Newton's Second Law, force is equal to the time derivative of this quantity. For 10 points, name this quantity, symbolized p, the product of mass and velocity.

In one of this author's novels, an inept journalist is sent to document "a very promising little war" in the fictional state of Ishmaelia. This author drew on his time working for the Daily Mail to write that novel about William Boot. The protagonist of another novel by this author learns of his wife Brenda's infidelity with John Beaver, and travels to South America, where is he is forced to read Dickens novels aloud to Todd. This author of Scoop wrote about Tony Last in A Handful of Dust, and about a visit to Lord Marchmain in Venice in a novel narrated by Sebastian Flyte's friend, Charles Ryder, and titled for an opulent estate in Wiltshire. For 10 points, name this English author of Brideshead Revisited.

The NTU method finds the product of the mass flow rate and this quantity. The product of volume, temperature, and coefficient of thermal expansion squared, divided by the isothermal compressibility, equals the difference between two forms of this property according to Mayer's relation. This property is equal to approximately 3R per mole of a crystalline substance according to the Dulong-Petit Law. The adiabatic index is the ratio between the values for this property at constant pressure and constant volume. The extensive form of this property has the same units as entropy, and can be found by dividing heat by temperature change. For 10 points, name this measure of the heat needed to raise the temperature of a substance by one degree Celsius.

An E-flat major piece by Louise Farrenc, written for this many instruments, is the largest ensemble for which she wrote chamber music. The standard instrumentation for an ensemble of this size originates from Louis Spohr's F major piece, titled Grand. Anton Webern used a tone row comprised of a trichord, its retrograde inversion, its retrograde, and its inversion, to write his Opus 24 Concerto for this many instruments. Aaron Copland's one-movement piece for this ensemble uses only string instruments. Franz Schubert's symphony of this number opens with a passage for two unaccompanied horns, and was actually the seventh symphony that he completed. However, according to the standard ordering, Schubert's symphony of this number directly follows the Unfinished Symphony. The most common ensemble of this size comprises a wind quintet plus one of each string instrument. For 10 points, give this number of instruments in a nonet.

One of these atoms with a positive charge is part of a reactant in the Corey-Chaykovsky reaction. A radioactive isotope of this element labeled capsid proteins in the Hershey-Chase experiment, and this element is part of the acid formed by the contact process. Crosslinks containing it can fuse different polymer chains so they cannot move independently, a process developed by Charles Goodyear and termed vulcanization. Cysteine features a thiol group, which contains this element. For 10 points, name this element in the same group as oxygen?

The composer Samuel Coleridge-Taylor used one of these works for his overture to Hiawatha's Wedding Feast. These songs inspired the third movement of a "Tone Journey" by Ferde Grofé ["FER-dee gro-FAY"] whose last section depicts Fat Tuesday. These works play the part of a chorale in a piece written in response to Kristallnacht, Michael Tippett's oratorio A Child of Our Time. Michael Steinberg claims that one of these songs inspired a flute solo in the first movement of a symphony in E minor, whose Largo second movement was adapted into one of these works by William Arms Fisher. These songs inspired Grofé's Mississippi Suite and Antonín Dvořák's Symphony No. 9 "From the New World." For 10 points, "Go Down Moses" and "Swing Low, Sweet Chariot?" are examples of what kind of religious songs created by African-Americans?
acceptableAnswers: prompt on answers like gospel songs

tossups.text: Projects Blue Book, Sign, and Grudge were studies of these things conducted by the U.S. Air Force. A supposed discovery of one of these things in Roswell, New Mexico was passed off as a weather balloon by the military. These objects that supposedly make crop circles are rumored to be studied at Area 51. For 10 points, name these unexplainable aerial phenomena often attributed to alien activity and described as flying saucers.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on weather balloons until mention

tossups.text: At the end of this novel, the pharmacist Homais receives a government decoration. A sex scene in this novel is narrated entirely from outside the cab in which it takes place. One character in this novel is reunited with a law student during a performance of Lucia di Lammermoor. In this work, the title character's husband botches a surgery while attempting to treat a club-footed man. The title character of this novel borrows money from Lheureux in order to continue her affairs with Rodolphe and Leon. That title character of this work swallows arsenic after going bankrupt. For 10 points, name this novel by Gustave Flaubert.

parts.text: Name this cycle of twenty-four erotic poems that its author penned while touring Italy in 1787.
The Roman Elegies are by this German writer, who penned the verse drama Faust and the novel The Sorrows of Young Werther.

Friedrich Schiller discussed Goethe in an essay that divides poets into "naïve" and this other category. This adjective partly titles a Gustave Flaubert novel about Frederic Moreau and his infatuation with Madame Arnoux.

bonuses.leadin: This cycle of poems was dedicated to Christiane Vulpius and begins "speak to me, stones, oh say, you lofty palaces, tell me!" For 10 points each:

parts.text: Corneille's tragedy Le Cid sparked a massive quarrel, since it violated three "Classical" unities supposedly derived from this work by Aristotle. This is the first Western treatise solely about literature.
The 17th-century French author Jean de la Fontaine is most famous for his hundreds of works in this genre. Other famous works in this genre were supposedly written by a slave named Aesop.
Madame de Sévigné wrote over a thousand of these works. Novels that claim to be constructed from these works include Frankenstein, Pamela, and The Sorrows of Young Werther.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about French literature in the 17th century, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Edmonia Lewis worked primarily in Rome in the 1870s, where she gained fame for sculpting this Egyptianqueen in the throes of death, having poisoned herself with an asp.
After moving to France in the 1890s, Henry Ossawa Tanner painted a scene of an old man teaching a littleboy to play this American instrument.
Tanner was the first Black American to exhibit at this French art museum; the second was Ealy Mays in2005. This museum is more famous for housingWingedVictoryand theMona Lisa.

bonuses.leadin: Black American artists like Edmonia Lewis and Henry Ossawa Tanner often worked in Europe to avoidrace-based prejudice. Answer the following about their work, for ten points each.

parts.text: This kind of dead-code elimination, which is most effective on ECMAScript modules, removes whole files or functions from dependencies when it can be statically determined that they're unused in a bundle.

Modern bundlers concatenate modules into fewer scopes when possible in an optimization named for this term applied to "scope." In a related optimization known by this term, JavaScript moves declarations of variables to the tops of their enclosing scopes.

Scope hoisting often leads to performance improvements since it performs this optimization on imported modules. This general compiler optimization replaces a function call with the code inside the function.

bonuses.leadin: Bundlers package together many files to create production builds of websites. Answer the following about optimizations they perform to reduce how much code must be sent over the wire, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Methods that devices can use to communicate with others devices on a network include Unicast, Multicast, and this third protocol, which sends a message to all networked devices.
This type of network address is used in conjunction with a MAC address. This type of address can also be subnetted in order to optimize the distribution of these addresses by a router.

The two primarily-used versions of Internet Protocol are IPv4 and IPv6. Although Ipv4 uses four sets of eight binary digits, IPv6 uses eight sets of digits from this number system in order to drastically increase the number of assignable addresses. In this number system, the highest value digit is F, with a value of 15.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about networking.

parts.text: Name this folk singer of "Like a Rolling Stone."

"Scarborough Fair" was a favorite of many songwriters, including Bob Dylan, who was inspired by a recording to write "Girl from the North Country." Identify the four plants mentioned in the second line of "Scarborough Fair."
Dylan listed among his musical influences this blues singer, who was known as the "Mother of Blues." She sang while Louis Armstrong played the trumpet on many songs by the Georgia Jazz Band.

bonuses.leadin: Thanks to this man winning a Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016, we're now allowed to write a non-trash bonus on him. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel turned into a 1985 Steven Spielberg film featuring Whoopi Goldberg as Celie.
The Color Purple is a novel by this author of The Temple of My Familiar.
This short story by Alice Walker depicts the tension between Mrs. Johnson's daughters Maggie and Wangero, the latter of whom fears Maggie will subject family quilts to the title action.

bonuses.leadin: In this epistolary novel, Celie's letters tell of her separation from her sister and her abusive marriage to Mister. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Puritan minister of the Old North Church, who claimed that "spectral evidence" was permissible during a series of 1692 events.
Cotton Mather played a pivotal role in the witchcraft trials of this New England town.
The Salem witch trials occurred in this colony. After arriving here, John Winthrop proclaimed a "city upon a hill".

bonuses.leadin: With his father Increase, he actively supported smallpox inoculation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This man was the Provisional President of the Republic of China for three months in 1912. He is still revered by people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, but his plans for a Republic were quickly frustrated.

This man was a Viceroy and a Minister under the Qing but then became the President after Sun Yat-Sen. He helped kill Sun Yat-Sen's Republican dream and had himself declared Emperor in 1916, but died a few months later.

Yuan Shikai feuded with the Guomingdang, which was later led by this man. He was commander of the Whampoa Military Academy and led the Northern Expedition in 1928. He ruled Taiwan until his death in 1975.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some leaders from China's Republican period FTPE:

parts.text: At the end of this Tolstoy novel, the title character ends her life by jumping in front of a moving train.
Taking place during the Crimean War, a major plot during this expansive novel is the marriage between Anna Pavlovna and Pierre Bezukhov.

Claimed by Ivan Bunin as one of the finest Russian works, this short novel deals with Dmitriy Olenin's befriending of one of the title characters, Eroshka, and the series of subsequent conflicts with the rival Chechens.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these other Leo Tolstoy works for ten points each:

parts.text: Name this ballet set in India, a collaboration between Marius Petipa and Ludwig Minkus. In its final scene, Solor is reunited with his lover Nikiya when a collapsing temple takes his life.
La Bayadère's "Kingdom of the Shades" scene also includes one of these dances for two performers. The "grand" variety of this dance is divided into five parts.

The female dancer performs thirty-two consecutive fouettés (fwee-TAYZ) at the climax of the pas de deux in Act III of this Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky ballet about Odette's transformation into the title bird.

bonuses.leadin: This ballet's "Kingdom of the Shades" scene is an opium-induced dream that begins with several dozen women making their way down a winding ramp performing repeated arabesques. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Islamic empire ruled by sultans such as Suleiman the Magnificent. It conquered Constantinople from the Byzantines in 1453 and was dissolved after World War I.
This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).

Shortly before its dissolution, the Ottoman Empire perpetrated a genocide against this ethnic group, in which around 1.5 million people were killed. This is the majority ethnic group in a modern-day country that borders Turkey to its east.

bonuses.leadin: This empire's expansion into Eastern Europe culminated with its unsuccessful 16th-century siege of Vienna. For 10 points each:

parts.text: First detected in 1971, these events originate in the outermost layer of the suns' atmosphere and are caused by magnetic reconnection. The shockwave from one of these large bursts of solar wind can cause geomagnetic storms much larger than those caused by solar flares.

On June 30, 1908 this event, which occurred near Lake Baikal, it produced shock waves that knocked people over hundreds of kilometers away. It was probably caused by the explosion of a meteoroid less than 10 kilometers above the ground.

In 1883, this Volcano, located on a namesake island on the Sunda Strait, erupted massively. The airborne debris from the eruption of this Indonesian volcano is thought to have caused brilliant sunsets.

bonuses.leadin: Things blow up sometimes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this long time companion of Spiros Antonopoulos. After Antonopoulos is confined to an asylum, this man, who is both deaf and mute, visits him until he dies.
John Singer appears in The Heart is a Lonely Hunter, a novel by this author of The Ballad of the Sad Cafe.
Carson McCullers accused this writer of To Kill a Mockingbird of "poaching on [her] literary preserves." Her only other novel, Go Set a Watchman, was controversially released in 2016.

bonuses.leadin: This character saves up money earned from working for a jeweller to buy a moving picture machine for his best friend. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this physicist, who with Dirac gives his name to a statistical distribution obeyed by half-integer-spin particles.
Fermi's name is also sometimes given to the coupling constant of this fundamental force, since he was one of the first to attempt to formulate a theory of it.
The Fermi level is the highest occupied energy level in a fermionic system; at zero temperature, it is equal to this thermodynamic quantity.

bonuses.leadin: This man's namesake surfaces are mapped by the de Haas-van Alphen effect, while his namesake "golden rule" is used to compute transition probabilities. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Named for the hero of an 1805 naval engagement, this 151 foot monument was designed by William Railton.
This Italian's many commemorative works include the 1829 Monument to the Stuarts and the pyramid-like Monument to the Archduchess Maria Christina in Vienna.
Commissioned by the Revolutionary Department of Fine Arts, this never realized Vladimir Tatlin structure would have stood more than 1300 feet if it was ever completed.
acceptableAnswers: The Monument to the Third International

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about some related works of art and their creators, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this operation that is performed along contours in complex analysis. This operation is the inverse of differentiation by the fundamental theorem of calculus.
This mathematician names an integral formula and residue theorem in complex analysis. With Bernhard Riemann, this mathematician names a set of equations satisfied by holomorphic functions.

Hermann Schwarz names an integral formula that writes a holomorphic function in terms of its real part along this object's boundary. The Riemann mapping theorem describes biholomorphic functions that map onto this object.

bonuses.leadin: The residue theorem is used to evaluate this operation around a region containing poles. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this city, nicknamed "Athens on the Prairie," which is home to many public works including Henry Moore's Large Arch and I. M. Pei's Cleo Rogers Memorial Library.
An architect from this country designed Columbus's Irwin Union Bank and Miller House as well as the TWA Flight Center. Another architect from this country founded the furniture company Artek.

Both Eero Saarinen and his father Eliel designed these buildings for Columbus, the latter of which features a 160-foot-tall tower. Antoni Gaudí died before completing one of these buildings, the Sagrada Família.

bonuses.leadin: J. Irwin Miller encouraged this city to adopt an international reputation for modernist architecture by financing buildings such as Robert Venturi's Fire Station No. 4. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this set of English civil wars fought between the houses of Lancaster and York.
King Richard died at this decisive battle of the Wars of the Roses.
After the wars of the roses, this monarch started the Tudor line of English kings.

bonuses.leadin: Two of the battles in them were the Battle of Tewkesbury and the Battle of Towton. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this cockney who acts as Mr Pickwick's valet in The Pickwick Papers.
The relationship between Weller and Pickwick has been likened to that between Sancho Panza and this knight who tilts at windmills.
This other Dickensian character employs a valet called "The Avenger" in the flat he shares with Herbert Pocket.
